activities.name: Travelling in the harmattan
activities.note: nothing closes; the harmattan is the dry season, and it is what makes the roads passable — the trade-off is the dust

windows.reason: the harmattan blows especially in December, January and February: its dust haze can severely limit visibility for days, and humidity can drop low enough to cause nosebleeds
the edges of the harmattan season, which runs from late November to mid-March: dry, with hazy skies when the dust is up

activities.name: Cure Salée and the Gerewol, In-Gall
activities.note: Tuareg and Wodaabe herders gather at the salt flats near In-Gall; the government fixes the date each year

windows.reason: held after the rains in September, usually in the last two weeks, with camel races and the Wodaabe Gerewol

activities.name: West African giraffes around Kouré
activities.note: in the dry season the herds range south toward the Dosso reserve and are much harder to find

windows.reason: the rainy season, early June to early September around Niamey, when the herd moves north into the bush around Kouré, about 80 km south-east of Niamey
